items.title: A copper ion is colourless — and blue, and green
items.claim: Anhydrous CuSO4 is white. Add water and it turns vivid blue. Dissolve in concentrated HCl and it goes yellow-green. Same copper ion, drastically different colours.
items.prompt: What changes when ligands swap around the same Cu2+ centre?

options.text: Different ligands split the d-orbitals by different energies, so the wavelengths of light absorbed change, and the colour observed is the complementary colour of that wavelength
Water and chloride dissolve the copper, removing the colour

items.reveal_title: Crystal field theory — the geometry of d-orbitals
items.reveal:
Cu2+ has 9 d-electrons. In an octahedral field of ligands, the five d-orbitals split into two sets separated by an energy gap (delta-octahedral). A d-electron absorbs a photon and is promoted across this gap.

The gap depends on the ligand — the spectrochemical series ranks them: I- less than Br- less than Cl- less than H2O less than NH3 less than CN-. Larger gaps absorb shorter wavelengths. Cu(H2O)6 2+ absorbs orange (delta corresponding to ~600 nm), so it transmits blue. CuCl4 2- has a smaller gap, absorbs red, transmits yellow-green.

Anhydrous Cu2+ in CuSO4 has no significant ligand field at all — no splitting big enough for visible absorption — and so the salt is white.
items.why: Colour is treated as a fixed property of an element. It's actually a property of the coordination environment around a single ion.

items.title: Fireworks colours are atomic fingerprints
items.claim: Lithium gives a red flame. Sodium gives orange. Potassium lilac. Copper blue-green. Strontium crimson. Each element produces a characteristic colour because electrons fall through fixed energy gaps.

options.text: Heating excites electrons; they fall back to lower energy levels, emitting photons of specific wavelengths set by the spacing of the atom's electron energy levels — colour is set by the element, not the flame
The shape of the metal sample
The amount of oxygen in the flame

items.reveal_title: Spectra are the unique signatures of atoms
items.reveal:
Each element has its own set of allowed electron energy levels — set by the quantum mechanics of its electrons and nucleus. A flame thermally excites electrons; as they relax, photons emerge with energies exactly equal to the gap between levels (E = hf).

Sodium's strong 'D line' at 589 nm (orange) is the 3p-to-3s transition. The bright yellow streetlights you see are sodium-vapour lamps using the same transition.

This is also how astronomers identify elements in stars they can never visit: they fit the dark or bright lines in stellar spectra to known atomic transition wavelengths. Helium was discovered in the Sun (1868) before being found on Earth (1895) using exactly this technique.
items.why: Flame colours look like a simple party trick. They are direct measurements of quantum-mechanical energy levels.

items.title: Gold is yellow because its electrons move at over half the speed of light
items.claim: Silver, copper and gold all sit in Group 11. Silver is shiny white, copper reddish, gold yellow. Gold's colour is a direct consequence of special relativity acting on its inner electrons.

options.text: Gold's 1s electrons move at about 58 percent the speed of light; relativistic mass increase contracts the 6s orbital and shrinks the 5d-to-6s gap into the visible — blue is absorbed, yellow is reflected
Gold's surface oxidises to a yellow film
Gold absorbs longer wavelengths because it is denser

items.reveal:
For silver (Z=47) the analogous d-to-s transitions sit in the ultraviolet; silver reflects all visible light evenly. For gold (Z=79) the energy gap collapses into the visible blue and absorbs around 470 nm. The complementary colour — yellow — is what bounces back at your eye.

The same relativistic 6s contraction weakens metallic bonding in mercury (Z=80), giving it a melting point of -39°C and making it the only metal liquid at room temperature.

Without special relativity, gold would be silvery white and mercury would be a solid metal like cadmium above it.
items.why: Colour is treated as an unchanging elemental property. For heavy elements it depends on relativistic effects on inner electrons.
